# SVGPathCommander

> A TypeScript sourced toolkit for manipulating the `d` (description) attribute of SVG `<path>` elements. Parses any path string into a `PathArray`, provides chainable instance and static methods for normalizing, optimizing, converting, transforming, reversing and morphing paths, plus accurate geometry queries. Works in browser and Node.js, ships strong TypeScript definitions and is verified against real Chromium by a Vitest + Playwright suite with 100% coverage.

## About

`svg-path-commander` is a modern set of TypeScript tools for manipulating the `d` attribute of `SVGPathElement` items. The library:

- parses any valid SVG path string (including shorthand commands) into a `PathArray` and serializes it back into a lossless path string;
- is implemented as a chainable `SVGPathCommander` class with instance methods, while every tool is also exposed as a standalone static method;
- converts between absolute / relative command sets, to cubic Bézier only (`pathToCurve`), and from other SVG shapes (`<circle>`, `<rect>`, `<polygon>`, `<polyline>`, `<line>`, `<ellipse>`) into `<path>` (`shapeToPath`);
- applies any CSS / SVG transform function to path commands via the modern `DOMMatrix` API (`@thednp/dommatrix` shim), including 3D to 2D projections, with SVG-consistent transform origins;
- reverses path draw direction without altering the path (`reversePath`), including specialized variants for `C`-only paths and for other shapes;
- provides more reliable and more accurate built-in `getBBox`, `getPointAtLength` and `getTotalLength` than the native methods, plus community tools like `getPropertiesAtLength`, `getSegmentOfPoint`, `isPointInStroke`, `pathsIntersection` and `boundingBoxIntersect`;
- returns the frame of the path at a given length — `getPropertiesAtLength` answers with the point, the unit tangent vector, the unit normal vector (the left normal of the tangent) and the angle of the tangent in degrees, next to the segment metadata;
- simplifies a path with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm — `simplifyPath` keeps the points that are needed to hold the shape of the path within a tolerance you choose, the result is a path of straight lines;
- resamples a path to a given number of points — `resamplePath` spreads the points evenly over the length of the path and keeps its corners, so the shape of the path keeps its vertices;
- offsets a path along its normals — `offsetPath` shifts the path to one side or outlines the stroke around it, with the `miter`, `bevel` and `round` joins and the `butt`, `square` and `round` caps of SVG; the side is literal, the left side is the left normal of the direction of travel, and the offset is not cleaned up, so a distance larger than the local radius of curvature produces a self-crossing curve;
- joins and splits the sub-paths of a path — `joinPath` concatenates two paths into one, `splitPath` cuts a path into its sub-paths and `reverseSubPath` reverses one of them;
- tells if a point is inside a filled shape — `isPointInPath` tests the point against the flattened path with the `nonzero` or the `evenodd` fill rule of the SVG `fill-rule` attribute, and a point on the boundary of the shape is inside of it, the way the browser answers it with `isPointInFill()`;
- supports path morphing via `equalize` / `equalizePaths` / `equalizeSegments` and per-segment interpolation through `samplePath` / `splitPath`; the `equalize` facade is the recommended entry point, it aligns the points of the two paths, normalizes their winding and places their points with the `segment` or the `arcLength` strategy;
- serves every geometry query from a shared length table — `getPropertiesAtLength`, `getPointAtLength` and the closest point search are linear in the number of segments instead of quadratic (a 4 000 segment path answers a length query in about 2 ms, and a closest point query in about 1 ms);
- has a defined answer for an empty or malformed path: a zeroed bounding box, a `{x:0,y:0}` point, `false`, `undefined` or a synthetic `["M", 0, 0]` segment, depending on the tool — and no tool modifies the data it is given;
- is built with [tsdown](https://tsdown.dev), producing ESM (`index.js`), UMD (`index.min.js`, global `SVGPathCommander`) and a static-methods-only `util.js` entry into `dist/`;
- ships four entry points, so a bundle only carries the tools it uses: `svg-path-commander` (everything), `svg-path-commander/util` (the tools), `svg-path-commander/morph` (the morphing engine) and `svg-path-commander/intersect` (the intersection engine); the JSR package has the same subpaths;
- is performance-oriented: allocation-free parsing and string output, a single-pass fast path for 2D transforms, and benchmarks against [SvgPath](https://github.com/fontello/svgpath) via `vpr bench` (results in the README);
- is JSR-ready: `deno.json` publishes the raw TypeScript source as `@thednp/svg-path-commander` with clean `deno check` / `deno lint` / `deno publish --dry-run`.

## Usage

```ts
import SVGPathCommander from "svg-path-commander";

const path = new SVGPathCommander("M0 0L100 0L50 100");
path.flipX().toString(); // "M0 0L100 0L50 -100"
```

```ts
import { getPathBBox, pathToCurve } from "svg-path-commander/util";

getPathBBox("M0 0L100 0L50 100"); // { x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100 }
```

```ts
import { equalize } from "svg-path-commander/morph";

const [eq1, eq2] = equalize("M0 0L100 0L50 100Z", "M0 0L100 0L100 100L0 100Z");
```

```ts
import { pathsIntersection } from "svg-path-commander/intersect";

pathsIntersection("M0 50C0 0,100 0,100 50", "M50 0C100 0,100 100,50 100", false);
```

```ts
import { offsetPath } from "svg-path-commander/util";

// the left side is the left normal of the direction of travel, "both" is the
// outline of the stroke
offsetPath("M0 0L100 0", 10); // [["M", 0, 10], ["L", 100, 10]]
offsetPath("M0 0L100 0", 10, { side: "both", join: "round", cap: "round" });
```

## API Overview

**Constructor** — accepts an SVG path string, a `PathArray` (array of command segments) or a generic array of numbers / strings; optional `Options` (e.g. `transformOrigin`, `rounding`) validated against `defaultOptions`.

**Instance methods** — chainable: `parse`, `toString`, `flipX`, `flipY`, `transform`, `scale`, `rotate`, `translate`, `skew`, `skewX`, `skewY`, `reverse`, `reverseSubPath`, `join`, `reverseC`, `toAbsolute`, `toRelative`, `toCurve`, `optimize`, `round`, `normalize`, `simplify`, `offset`, `getPointAtLength`, `getPropertiesAtLength`, `getSegmentOfPoint`, `getIntersections`, `getBBox`, `getTotalLength`, `isPointInPath`.

**Getters** — `bbox`, `length`, `string`, `segments`, `path`, `options`.

**Static methods** — `parsePathString`, `pathToString`, `normalizePath`, `optimizePath`, `simplifyPath`, `offsetPath`, `resamplePath`, `pathToAbsolute`, `pathToRelative`, `pathToCurve`, `shapeToPath`, `shapeToPathArray`, `reversePath`, `reverseSubPath`, `joinPath`, `reverseCurve`, `transformPath`, `roundPath`, `splitPath`, `fixPath`, `getPathBBox`, `getPathArea`, `getDrawDirection`, `getTotalLength`, `getPointAtLength`, `getSegmentAtLength`, `getSegmentOfPoint`, `getPropertiesAtLength`, `getPropertiesAtPoint`, `getClosestPoint`, `isPointInStroke`, `isPointInPath`, `isValidPath`, `pathsIntersection`, `boundingBoxIntersect`, `equalize`, `equalizePaths`, `equalizeSegments`, plus the low-level tools in the `svg-path-commander/util` subpath entry.

**Entry points** — `svg-path-commander` holds the class and every static method, `svg-path-commander/util` holds the tools, `svg-path-commander/morph` holds the morphing engine (`equalize`, `equalizePaths`, `equalizeSegments`, `resamplePath`, `fixPath`, `splitCubicSegment`) and `svg-path-commander/intersect` holds the intersection engine (`pathsIntersection`, `boundingBoxIntersect`, `isPointInsideBBox`).

**Types** — `PathArray`, `PathSegment`, `PathCommand`, `AbsoluteCommand`, `RelativeCommand`, `NormalSegment`, `IteratorCallback`, `Options`, `TransformObject`, `PathBBox`, `ShapePath`, `ShapeAttrs`, `OffsetOptions`, `OffsetSide`, `OffsetJoin`, `OffsetCap`, `PointInPathOptions`, `FillRule`, `EqualizationOptions`, `EqualizeOptions`, and per-command segment aliases (`MSegment`, `LSegment`, `CSegment`, `ArcSegment`, ...).

## Key Differences

- Works in **Node.js** and browsers — no `SVGPathElement` required for path computation (the `@thednp/dommatrix` shim covers `DOMMatrix`).
- All transformations are consistent with the SVG coordinate system, including `transformOrigin` for rotation.
- The built-in `getBBox`, `getTotalLength` and `getPointAtLength` are implemented mathematically (arcs via Gauss-Legendre quadrature) and are more accurate than the native methods.
- Static methods return safe defaults for empty / invalid input (e.g. `getPathBBox("")` returns a zeroed box) while the constructor throws a `TypeError` on invalid path strings.
- The class API and the static methods share the same implementation, so behavior is identical whichever entry you use.
- The version is exposed as `SVGPathCommander.version` and follows `package.json`.
